headline: Crude Backs Off Its Highs as Traders Watch Iran Diplomacy
body_html:
Markets approach the opening bell in a cautious mood. Asian stocks traded warily overnight, and Brent crude slipped back from a six-month high on hopes that hostilities tied to the Iran conflict may ease. The relief looks fragile: the Houthis claimed fresh attacks on Saudi oil pumping stations and Riyadh's airport, and an intelligence memo warned that Iran has stepped up efforts to target American personnel.

Friday's session left stocks on the back foot. Of 544 stocks tracked, 339 fell and 199 rose. Energy stood out, up 2.72%, and semiconductors edged up 0.18%, while consumer shares lost 1.59% and materials 0.87%. Robert Half jumped 21.74%, with CrowdStrike gaining 8.25% and Zscaler 7.31%. On the downside, Corcept Therapeutics sank 20.13%, Bloom Energy fell 11.24% and Credo Technology dropped 9.51%.

At the open, watch whether energy holds its lead as crude retreats. Officials from the Mecca pact countries are due to meet Iranian counterparts in Tehran today, which could offer a read on de-escalation. Traders will also weigh the Bank of Japan's firm-toned decision to hold, which keeps a December rate rise in play, and President Trump's promise of a Canada tariff deal soon.

briefs.headline: Brent Retreats From Six-Month Peak
briefs.body: Crude oil pulled back from near its highest level in six months as investors bet that fighting linked to Iran could cool. Energy shares led Friday's session with a 2.72% gain, so the open will test whether that strength holds as oil eases.

briefs.headline: Houthi Claims Raise Stakes for Saudi Infrastructure
briefs.body: The Houthis said they struck Saudi oil pumping stations and Riyadh's airport as fighting intensified. The claims run against the more hopeful tone in crude and leave energy traders weighing supply risks against talk of easing hostilities.

briefs.headline: Tehran Meeting Is a Diplomatic Marker for Monday
briefs.body: Officials from the Mecca pact countries are set to meet Iranian officials in Tehran today. Any sign of progress could feed the hopes of de-escalation that have helped pull oil back from its recent highs, while a stall may bring the premium back.

briefs.headline: Bank of Japan Holds but Keeps a December Hike Alive
briefs.body: The Bank of Japan paused in a tone that analysts read as firm, leaving room to raise rates in December. Asian stocks traded cautiously overnight, and currency and bond moves tied to Tokyo's policy path are worth watching into the U.S. open.

briefs.headline: Cybersecurity Names Shine in a Weak Tape
briefs.body: Even with 339 of 544 tracked stocks falling Friday, security software stood apart. CrowdStrike rose 8.25% and Zscaler gained 7.31%, helping software finish only 0.11% lower. Traders will see whether buyers follow through at the open.

briefs.headline: Canada Tariff Deal Promised 'Soon' at Michigan Rally
briefs.body: President Trump told a crowd at a Michigan border rally that an agreement with Canada on tariffs is coming shortly. No terms were given, so industrial and consumer shares, both lower Friday, may react to any detail that emerges today.
